decisions.reason: As an own-page extension of the established psychiatric and therapeutic portfolio, the evening day-patient program remains strategically attractive and worth retaining while demand, staffing fit, and reimbursement continue to become clearer.

The carpentry workshop is more market-exposed than core care services, but it uses the firm's sheltered-workshop and training capabilities and is still a reasonable option to keep open for further learning.
Outpatient sociotherapy is very close to the firm's core support offer and relatively flexible to scale, so management would keep this low-commitment service on the market.
Counseling for senior living is tightly aligned with the firm's eldercare expertise, likely requires limited fixed investment, and therefore has little reason to be withdrawn.
The retail shop remains the most peripheral and uncertain offer, but it supports the sheltered-workshop model and social mission, so it is still worth keeping unless weak results become clearer.

Meal delivery for seniors is close to the firm's eldercare activities and offers service synergies, so despite logistical costs and competitive uncertainty it is sensible to retain this young option for now.
